title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover thresholds to reduce thrashing
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: During a recent incident we observed SLO enforcer thrashing when multiple regions reported transient latency spikes. The existing backoff and circuit-breaker thresholds compounded ordering issues in the enforcer queue which caused repeated regional failovers and client-visible request drops. This hotfix tightens threshold hysteresis, fixes an ordering edge in the backoff queue, and improves metrics/alerts to make the behavior observable in production.

What this change does: 1) Increases the smoothing window used by SLO violation rate calculations from 30s to 60s for regional decisions to reduce sensitivity to short spikes. 2) Adds a minimum backoff interval and linear jitter to regional circuit-breaker reopen attempts to avoid synchronized retries across regions. 3) Fixes an ordering bug where enforcer jobs could be re-enqueued out-of-order when a region transitions from degraded->healthy during concurrent evaluation. 4) Adds targeted unit and integration tests that reproduce the earlier thrashing pattern. 5) Adds a canary config and dashboard panel to the observability pack so we can watch reopen rates and effective backoff per region.

Rollout plan: This is a hotfix that should be deployed to Dedicated and Hosted canaries first, monitored for 24 hours, then promoted to all regions. If reopen rates remain elevated after 24h the previous thresholds can be restored via runtime flags.

Checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for backoff ordering - [x] Add integration smoke test that simulates staggered regional spikes - [x] Add telemetry for reopen_rate and effective_backoff_seconds - [x] Update canary config - [x] Run canary in staging and production canaries

Related: SUP-4421 (customer report), ENG-2789 (SLO enforcer hardening), internal incident runbook reference.
